How Ukraine’s Killer Drones Are Beating Russian Jamming
Killer drones spot landmarks as they fly to their targets
Tereza Pultarova
21h
10 min read
Horizontal
Ukrainian troops tested KrattWorks' Ghost Dragon drone in Estonia last year.
KrattWorks
Ukraine’s 1 June attack
on multiple Russian military bases destroyed or damaged as many as 41 Russian aircraft, including some of the country’s most advanced bombers. Estimates of the sum total of the damage range from US $2 billion to $7 billion. Supposedly planned for a
year and a half
, the Ukrainian operation was exceptional in its sophistication: Ukrainian agents reportedly smuggled dozens of first-person-view attack
drones
into
Russia
on trucks,
situating them close to the air bases
where the target aircraft were vulnerable on tarmacs. The bases included one in Irkutsk, 4,300 kilometers from
Ukraine
, and another in south Murmansk, 1,800 km away. Remote pilots in Ukraine then launched the killer drones simultaneously.
The far-reaching operation was being hailed as the most inventive and bold of the war so far. Indeed,
IEEE Spectrum
has been regularly covering the ascent of Ukraine’s military drone programs, both
offensive
and
defensive
, and for
air
,
marine
, and
land
missions. In this article, originally posted on April 6, we described another bold Ukrainian drone initiative, which was applying artificial intelligence-based navigational software to enable killer drones to navigate to targets even in the presence of heavy
jamming
.
After the Estonian startup
KrattWorks
dispatched the first batch of its
Ghost Dragon ISR
quadcopters
to Ukraine in mid-2022, the company’s officers thought they might have six months or so before they’d need to reconceive the drones in response to new battlefield realities. The 46-centimeter-wide flier was far more robust than the hobbyist-grade
UAVs
that came to define the
early days of the drone war
against Russia. But within a scant three months, the Estonian team realized their painstakingly fine-tuned device had already become obsolete.
Related:
Ukraine Tech Turns Combat into Real-Life “Game”
Rapid advances in
jamming
and
spoofing
—the only efficient defense against drone attacks—set the team on an unceasing marathon of innovation. Its latest technology is a neural-network-driven optical navigation system, which allows the drone to continue its mission even when all radio and satellite-navigation links are jammed. It began tests in
Ukraine
in December, part of a trend toward jam-resistant,
autonomous UAVs
(uncrewed aerial vehicles). The new fliers herald yet another phase in the unending struggle that pits drones against the jamming and
spoofing
of
electronic warfare,
which aims to sever links between drones and their operators. There are now
tens of thousands
of jammers straddling the front lines of the war, defending against drones that are not just killing soldiers but also destroying armored vehicles, other drones,
industrial infrastructure
, and even tanks.
During tests near Kyiv, Ukraine, in 2024, a technician prepared to release a drone outfitted with software by Auterion.
Justyna Mielnikiewicz
“The situation with
electronic warfare
is moving extremely fast,” says Martin Karmin, KrattWorks’ cofounder and chief operations officer. “We have to constantly iterate. It’s like a cat-and-mouse game.”
I met Karmin at the company’s headquarters in the outskirts of Estonia’s capital, Tallinn. Just a couple of hundred kilometers to the east is the tiny nation’s border with Russia, its former oppressor. At 38, Karmin is barely old enough to remember what life was like under Russian rule, but he’s heard plenty. He and his colleagues, most of them volunteer members of the
Estonian Defense League
, have “no illusions” about
Russia
, he says with a shrug.
His company is as much about arming
Estonia
as it is about helping Ukraine, he acknowledges. Estonia is not officially at war with Russia, of course, but regions around the border between the two countries have for years been subjected to persistent jamming of satellite-based
navigation systems
, such as the
European Union’s Galileo satellites
, forcing occasional flight cancellations at Tartu airport. In November,
satellite
imagery revealed that Russia is expanding its military bases along the Baltic states’ borders.
“We are a small country,” Karmin says. “Innovation is our only chance.”
Navigating by Neural Network
In KrattWorks’ spacious, white-walled workshop, a handful of engineers are testing software. On the large ocher desk that dominates the room, a selection of KrattWorks’ devices is on display, including a couple of fixed-wing, smoke-colored UAVs designed to serve as aerial decoys, and the Ghost Dragon ISR
quadcopter
, the company’s flagship product.
Now in its third generation, the Ghost Dragon has come a long way since 2022. Its original command-and-control-band
radio
was quickly replaced with a smart frequency-hopping system that constantly scans the av

data.title: Ubicloud: Open-Source Alternative to AWS
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: Ubicloud是一个开源云平台，提供类似AWS的弹性计算、块存储、防火墙、负载均衡、托管Postgres和IAM等基础设施即服务（IaaS）功能。它可以运行在Hetzner、Leaseweb和AWS Bare Metal等裸金属提供商上，用户可以选择自行设置或使用Ubicloud的管理服务。平台允许用户构建自己的云环境，通过控制平面管理裸金属Linux机器，并提供便捷的VM创建和管理功能。相比公共云提供商，Ubicloud具有开放源码、成本更低和更强的控制权等优势，适合需要可移植性、安全性和合规性的应用场景。当前，Ubicloud实现了AWS约10%的服务功能，但覆盖了80%的常用场景，特别适合CI/CD管道等临时工作负载和简单的应用部署服务。用户可通过社区论坛获取支持和反馈。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenStack替代方案中的技术选择和功能需求

不同观点：
• [技术选型的质疑] Daviey对选择Ruby开发OpenStack替代方案表示好奇和质疑。他提到Python在OpenStack早期项目Nova中的使用虽然加快了开发进度，但后期出现了性能问题，尤其是在并发处理上。Daviey认为如果今天重新选择，可能会选择Golang或Rust，因为它们在性能和并发处理上更有优势，并对选择Ruby表示不解。
  
• [对开源替代品的怀疑] sidcool对将任何声称是AWS开源替代品的项目持怀疑态度，暗示对该项目能否真正与AWS竞争缺乏信心，语气中带有嘲讽。

• [功能需求的提问] aitchnyu关注实际使用中的功能需求，提出了关于虚拟机（VM）的1G内存 hobby tiers、Postgres数据库的1G内存方案以及对象存储的可用性问题。同时，他还关心VM的定时备份和按需备份功能的具体情况。

补充讨论：
• Daviey对Python在OpenStack中使用后的性能问题提出了具体例子，并以此为基础推导出对Ruby技术选型的质疑。
• sidcool的评论虽然简短，但反映了对项目整体可行性的怀疑态度，属于对项目定位的宏观批评。
• aitchnyu的评论聚焦于实际应用场景中的具体功能需求，特别是资源限制较小的hobby tiers和备份功能的实现情况，显示出用户对产品细节的关注。

争议焦点：
• 技术选型的合理性，特别是在性能和并发处理上，Ruby是否适合用于OpenStack替代方案的开发存在争议。
• 项目是否能够真正成为AWS的开源替代品，sidcool的评论暗示了对这一目标的怀疑。

总结：评论主要围绕技术选型和功能需求展开，Daviey质疑Ruby的选择，sidcool对项目定位表示怀疑，而aitchnyu则关注具体功能实现。

Ubicloud
Ubicloud is an open source cloud that can run anywhere. Think of it as an open alternative
to cloud providers, like what Linux is to proprietary operating systems.
Ubicloud provides IaaS cloud features on bare metal providers, such as Hetzner, Leaseweb,
and AWS Bare Metal. You can set it up yourself on these providers or you can use our
managed service
.
Quick start
Managed platform
You can use Ubicloud without installing anything. When you do this, we pass along the
underlying provider's benefits to you, such as price or location.
https://console.ubicloud.com
Build your own cloud
You can also build your own cloud. To do this, start up Ubicloud's control plane and
connect to its cloud console.
git clone git@github.com:ubicloud/ubicloud.git
# Generate secrets for demo
./demo/generate_env
# Run containers: db-migrator, app (web & respirate), postgresql
docker-compose -f demo/docker-compose.yml up
# Visit localhost:3000
The control plane is responsible for cloudifying bare metal Linux machines.
The easiest way to build your own cloud is to lease instances from one of those
providers. For example:
https://www.hetzner.com/sb
Once you lease instance(s), run the following script for each instance to cloudify
the instance. By default, the script cloudifies bare metal instances leased from
Hetzner. After you cloudify your instances, you can provision and manage cloud
resources on these machines.
# Enter hostname/IP and provider, and install SSH key as instructed by script
docker exec -it ubicloud-app ./demo/cloudify_server
Later when you create VMs, Ubicloud will assign them IPv6 addresses. If your ISP
doesn't support IPv6, please use a VPN or tunnel broker such as Mullvad or Hurricane
Electric's
https://tunnelbroker.net/
to connect. Alternatively, you could lease
IPv4 addresses from your provider and add them to your control plane.
Why use it
Public cloud providers like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud have made life easier for
start-ups and enterprises. But they are closed source, have you rent computers
at a huge premium, and lock you in. Ubicloud offers an open source alternative,
reduces your costs, and returns control of your infrastructure back to you. All
without sacrificing the cloud's convenience.
Today, AWS offers about two hundred cloud services. Ultimately, we will implement
10% of the cloud services that make up 80% of that consumption.
Example workloads and reasons to use Ubicloud today include:
You have an ephemeral workload like a CI/CD pipeline (we're integrating with
GitHub Actions), or you'd like to run compute/memory heavy tests. Our managed
cloud is ~3x cheaper than AWS, so you save on costs.
You want a portable and simple app deployment service like
Kamal
. We're moving Ubicloud's control plane
from Heroku to Kamal; and we want to provide open and portable services for
Kamal's dependencies in the process.
You have bare metal machines sitting somewhere. You'd like to build your own
cloud for portability, security, or compliance reasons.
Status
You can provide us your feedback, get help, or ask us questions regarding your
Ubicloud installations in the
Community Forum
.

data.title: The rise of judgement over technical skill
data.author: kohlhofer
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了音乐人Brian Eno在1995年对计算机音序器的观察，以及其对当今AI时代的启示。Eno认为，音序器降低了技能的门槛，强调了判断力的重要性。如今，AI工具正在 democratizing 各种创意和专业任务，如写作、图像生成、编程和数据分析，技术壁垒逐渐消失。关键区别不在于能否完成任务，而在于判断力：知道该做什么、做出有意义的选择、评估质量以及理解背景。随着AI发展，未来工作将更侧重于战略判断，能够提出正确问题、有效界定问题、做出明智决策并指导AI工具的人将最具价值。Eno的观察为AI时代如何取得成功提供了蓝图。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在软件开发和其它领域中的作用与局限，特别是关于判断力与技术技能的关系

不同观点：
• ben30：认为AI在代码生成中的瓶颈不在于代码生成本身，而在于问题分解和代码审查两项需要深度判断的任务。AI可以帮助完成这些任务，但它们本质上仍是需要人类判断的问题。
• tingle：引用达芬奇的观点，强调判断力超越作品是好的迹象，年轻画家若具备这种 rare disposition 将达到完美。这里隐含了对人类判断力和经验的重视。
• physicsguy：将AI的讨论与教育中的批判性分析能力对比，认为没有一定的基础知识和心智模型，无法处理复杂问题。同时批评企业技术决策不当，导致开发瓶颈。
• nluken：批评科技行业用“民主化”来掩盖“降低入门门槛”的现实，认为这种说法带有道德伪装。
• TrackerFF：认为AI可以提供起点和大局观，但在处理 obscure 问题时仍会产生过时代码，实现上存在不足。
• mehulashah：指出领导等角色通过判断力扩展影响力，技术技能可能随时间 fade，但判断力使他们有效。
• scj：强调技术知识与判断力相辅相成，AI设计的蓝图可能在外观上吸引人，但若无法实现功能，则判断力不足。
• lordnacho：认为技术发展不断移动判断与技术技能的边界，AI只是移动了 goalposts，要求更高的 overview 和判断力。
• CleverLikeAnOx：批评文章冗余，认为若作者亲自打字，可能不会写出这样多余的结论。
• red_admiral：指出需要有经验的人来做AI尚不能做的工作，例如系统架构设计。
• 0x445442：以音乐创作为例，强调良好的判断力需要长时间的基础投入。
• overfl0w：引用阿西莫夫的《Jokester》故事，讨论提出正确问题的重要性。
• wg0：认为判断力基于技能，必须先掌握技能，才能做出判断，这是人类成功的根本。
• layer8：提出当AI在判断力和技术技能上超越普通人时，真正的挑战才会显现。
• dcre：批评文章对Eno引用的处理，认为文章后续部分降低了整体质量，显示作者判断力不足。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI是否真正能替代人类的判断力与技术技能，以及在AI辅助下，人类应如何提升自身能力。
• 判断力与技术知识的关系被反复提及，多数观点认为两者不可分割，AI只是改变了它们的应用范围和要求。
• 企业决策与教育中的批判性思维也被引入讨论，显示出AI影响不仅限于技术领域，还涉及到更广泛的应用场景。

44153732.article_content:
A version of this post was first published on
MapsAll
.
In 1995, musician and producer Brian Eno made a profound observation about computer sequencers that has become increasingly relevant in our AI-powered world:
“The great benefit of computer sequencers is that they remove the issue of skill, and replace it with the issue of judgement. With Cubase or Photoshop, anybody can actually do anything, and you can make stuff that sounds very much like stuff you’d hear on the radio, or looks very much like anything you see in magazines. So the question becomes not whether you can do it or not, because any drudge can do it if they’re prepared to sit in front of the computer for a few days, the question then is, ‘Of all the things you can now do, which do you choose to do?’”
The Parallel to AI
Eno’s insight perfectly captures what’s happening with AI tools today. Just as computer sequencers democratized music production, AI is democratizing a wide range of creative and professional tasks:
Writing and content creation
Image generation and design
Code development
Data analysis
Problem-solving
The technical barriers that once separated amateurs from professionals are rapidly dissolving. Anyone with access to AI tools can now produce work that, at least superficially, resembles professional output.
The New Differentiator: Judgement
As Eno predicted, the key differentiator is no longer technical skill but judgement. When everyone can generate content, code, or designs, the real value lies in:
Knowing what to create
: Understanding what’s worth making in the first place
Making meaningful choices
: Selecting the right approach from countless possibilities
Evaluating quality
: Distinguishing between good and great outputs
Understanding context
: Applying the right solution to the right problem
The Future of Work
As AI continues to evolve, we’ll see more roles shift from technical execution to strategic judgement. The most valuable professionals will be those who can:
Ask the right questions
Frame problems effectively
Make sound decisions
Provide meaningful direction to AI tools
Conclusion
Eno’s observation from nearly 30 years ago has become a blueprint for thriving in the AI era. The question is no longer “Can you do it?” but “What should you do, and why?” As technical barriers continue to fall, our ability to exercise good judgement becomes our most valuable asset.

data.title: 'It's thrilling': almost three centuries of the Belfast News Letter go online
data.author: thm
data.article_summary: 《贝尔法斯特新闻信》（Belfast News Letter）是世界上最古老的持续出版的英文日报，其现存最早一期可追溯至1738年10月3日。该报的数字化项目已完成，公众可通过图书馆或在线订阅免费访问其近三个世纪的存档内容，涵盖从克里米亚战争到北爱尔兰问题等重大历史事件。最早的版本仅两页，包含国际新闻、信件及转载内容，广告是唯一的插图。尽管初期版面简朴，但充满趣闻、八卦和耸动故事。该报曾被认为率先在欧洲报道美国独立宣言，但实际上晚于伦敦的两家报纸。其早期内容多为国际新闻， censorship严格，但仍包含许多引人入胜的故事。

44167462.article_content:
The earliest surviving edition of the Belfast News Letter, published 3 October 1738.
Photograph: British Library Board/Northern Ireland Office
View image in fullscreen
The earliest surviving edition of the Belfast News Letter, published 3 October 1738.
Photograph: British Library Board/Northern Ireland Office
Newspapers
‘It’s thrilling’: almost three centuries of the Belfast News Letter go online
The surviving editions of the world’s oldest, continuously published English-language daily can now be accessed free
Michael Savage
Media editor
Sun 1 Jun 2025 01.00 EDT
Last modified on Sun 1 Jun 2025 13.31 EDT
Share
T
here was a packed news agenda on 3 October 1738. The father of the notorious highwayman Dick Turpin had been arrested after being found with a stolen horse. Cannon fire rang out in St Petersburg to mark a Russian victory over the Ottoman Empire. In America, four families had been killed in Virginia in clashes with Native Americans. Meanwhile, a horse fell in the Thames at Westminster, nearly causing a drowning.
Welcome to the pages of the Belfast News Letter, where updates on the French Revolution run alongside adverts for brandy and the American Declaration of Independence was reported as a contemporary event.
The 3 October copy has a special place in newspaper history – it stakes a claim as the oldest surviving edition of the world’s longest continuously published English language daily newspaper. In fact, the paper is so old that it predates the the British empire’s switch to the Gregorian calendar. The edition would have been published on 14 October according to modern dating.
For the first time, the News Letter’s coverage of the most momentous events of the past three centuries can now be accessed free by anyone with a library pass or an online subscription, after the completion of a project to digitise its surviving editions. Everything from the Crimean war to the Troubles in
Northern Ireland
are covered, thanks to the joint project between the Northern Ireland Office, the British Library and online platform, Findmypast.
While the earliest editions are austere in appearance, Ben Lowry, the Belfast News Letter’s current editor, said they had many of the ingredients of the modern-day newspaper. “They look so severe that they’re like a reminder of an almost ancient age of poverty and hangings,” he said. “But actually, you see the genesis of newspapers in them. They’re full of fun. They have gossip. They have salacious stories.”
The first edition was probably published in 1737, some 60 years before the Act of Union and 175 years before the sinking of the Titanic, a major news event for a paper published in the city where the doomed liner was built.
View image in fullscreen
At the British Library, its chief executive Rebecca Lawrence, Northern Ireland secretary Hilary Benn (centre) and DC Thomson deputy chair Richard Hall view digitised Belfast News Letters.
Photograph: British Library Board/Northern Ireland Office
The American Declaration of Independence, reproduced in its 27 August 1776 edition, featured alongside adverts for books, an appeal for a lost watch and a reward for finding a stolen horse – one guinea for finding it, or three for delivering the horse and thief. Adverts were the only items featuring illustrations at the time. Theft was denoted by woodcut prints of the devil.
It was once thought that its publication of the declaration was a Europe-wide scoop. The editor sneaked a peek at the document as it travelled to London via Northern Ireland – or so the story goes. Like other journalistic stories of triumph, it appears the tale may have grown in the telling. In truth, two London papers, the St James Chronicle and the General Evening Post, had already printed the historic text a week earlier.
While the paper was dominated by world events, even the oldest editions have examples of unusual yarns too good to leave out. The 20 April 1739 edition carried a lengthy piece about a marriage near Dunluce, County Antrim, at which the bride was so drunk she demanded to go to bed the moment the ceremony had been completed, only to fall and break her nose. She was later spotted in bed with a man who was not the groom.
The oldest surviving edition recounts the dramatic tale of an Italian woman who stabbed and killed a man who had been harassing her for 18 months.
The earliest copies ran across just two pages and were largely made up of letters from around the world, or material relayed from other sources. “There was a lot more censorship during this early period,” said Beth Gaskell, lead curator of news and moving image at the British Library. “There’s a bigger focus on international news and a lot of verbatim reporting of events. There’s less opinion because it was dangerous. But that doesn’t mean that you don’t get these kinds of really interesting stories.”

data.title: If you are useful, it doesn't mean you are valued
data.author: weltview
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：职场中“有用性”（useful）和“价值”（valued）的区别及其影响

不同观点：
• [hn_throwaway_99] 认为用“有用”和“价值”来描述职场中的情况并不恰当。他指出，一个人在某个角色中表现出色并不意味着在另一个角色中也能如此。在商业关系中，几乎每个人都是“有用”的，所谓的“价值”会随着商业环境的变化而改变，如近期的科技行业裁员事件所示。

• [mboto] 强调了家庭生活对职场行为的潜移默化影响。他认为，如果在家庭中未被重视或边界被侵犯，这种模式可能会在职场中重现。提高自我意识和技能是解决问题的关键，心理治疗和交易分析可以帮助解决这些问题。

• [schmookeeg] 分享了自己的职业经历，表示自己在技术岗位上感到舒适和有用，但对商业角色没有兴趣。他认为可以选择简单地做一个有用的人，而不必追求所谓的价值或晋升。

• [bravesoul2] 表示在多个职场经历中，只有家人真正重视自己，企业并不会。他认为商业关系不可靠，应更注重家庭、健康等其他方面。

• [dinetrimr] 讲述了自己离开高薪工作后寻找“价值”的艰难经历，表示在当前市场环境下，感到既没有价值也没有用武之地，强调了工作稳定和健康保险等实际问题的重要性。

• [mergy] 认为“有用”和“价值”的区别在组织中并不总是清晰明确，组织动态变化快，个人需要不断评估自己的处境，并决定自己能接受的生活和工作状态。

• [47282847] 引用了一位将军的观点，区分了四种类型的职场人物，强调了聪明且懒惰的人适合领导角色，而愚蠢且勤奋的人则需警惕。

• [austin-cheney] 强调了在职场中能力与交付的重要性，指出软技能和沟通能力往往比努力工作更重要。有时雇主会故意限制员工的价值，使其成为商品。

• [ChrisMarshallNY] 分享了自己在日本公司工作的经历，表示尽管自己被重视，但由于文化差异，并未被充分纳入战略制定过程，认为“有用”和“价值”的定义需因地制宜。

• [submeta] 观察到许多踏实工作的员工并未得到应有的回报，而一些擅长表现和使用流行词汇的人则不断获得晋升，强调了自我表现和外界认知的影响。

• [LeifCarrotson] 用“财富之河”的比喻说明了在职场中，有用的贡献和获取回报之间的关系，指出有时贡献与回报并不成正比，需要策略和 leverage 来获取应得的回报。

• [bko] 认为不应将“价值”狭义地定义为晋升到管理或战略角色，许多工程师更愿意专注于技术工作，建议与管理层进行坦诚对话以设定合理的期望。

• [dotdi] 分享了自己在职场中感到有用但未被真正重视的经历，表示尽管薪酬不错，但感到职业发展停滞，最终选择了离职。

• [nubinetwork] 自嘲自己的20年职业生涯仅仅是“占位符”，对自我价值感到怀疑。

• [apples_oranges] 表示宁愿做一个有用的人，只要薪酬不错，不被邀请参加某些会议反而是种幸运。除非涉及股权和不良决策。

补充讨论：
- 职场中的“有用”和“价值”的定义和评估标准因人而异，且受组织动态、文化背景和个人期望的影响。
- 自我意识、家庭影响、软技能、以及外界认知在职场成功中起着重要作用。
- 职业发展和个人满足感之间的平衡是许多人面临的挑战，需要不断评估和调整。
- 商业环境的变幻莫测使得工作稳定性和实际福利（如健康保险）成为重要的考量因素。

data.title: Writing your own C++ standard library part 2
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了作者为了兴趣而编写的一个简化版C++标准库。文章澄清了两个主要误解：第一，该项目并非试图实现完整的ISO C++标准库，而是一个包含大多数应用所需的基本功能和类型的库；第二，关于将C++标准库称为"STL"的争论，作者指出这种用法在某些圈子中是常见的，尽管技术上不准确。

作者还讨论了容器实现的复杂性，指出通过限制类型行为良好（如要求noexcept移动），可以大幅简化代码。对于字符串分割等功能，作者提供了类似于Python的接口，并通过返回不同类型和使用回调函数来实现灵活性。

目前，该项目包含基本的字符串、正则表达式和容器功能，并已发布在代码库中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C++中循环结构与迭代器的实现及其复杂性，以及C++语言整体设计的讨论。

不同观点：
• **comex的观点**：认为在没有宏的情况下，将自定义类型与原生循环结构集成是可行的，但有些丑陋。通过实现`begin()`和`end()`方法，可以模拟Python式的迭代器协议，但需要临时存储每个项目，这会带来轻微的性能开销，不过编译器通常可以优化掉。

• **tialaramex的观点**：质疑某些C++标准库实现者对语言的全面理解，认为C++语言的复杂性已超出个人能够完全掌握的范围。指出C++的语法和语义非常重要，但在实际使用中，人们对其理解更像是对自然语言的理解，而不是像Perl或Rust那样严谨。

• **azhenley的观点**：提到帖子被Hackernews和Reddit转载后，多数评论偏离了实际内容，集中在两个附带问题上。

• **monkeyelite的观点**：比较了Python和C++的迭代器，指出Python迭代器简单但功能较少，例如不能轻松修改容器，而在C++中相当于InputIterator。

• **jandrewrogers的观点**：主张一个纯粹的C++20标准库，从第一原则重新设计，可以极大提升C++语言的价值和声誉。认为在某些时候，新的代码库不应再被兼容性负担拖累。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是C++的复杂性和理解问题，特别是对标准库实现者的质疑，以及语言设计中兼容性与创新的矛盾。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是不同语言之间迭代器功能的比较，以及在C++中实现自定义迭代器的技术细节和性能考虑。
• 评论中也反映出社区对讨论主题偏离的倾向，以及对外部讨论平台评论质量的评价。

这些观点共同勾勒出C++语言在实际应用和设计中的多重挑战，包括技术实现、语言复杂性和社区认知等方面。

44142359.article_content:
This blog post
talked about the "self written C++ standard library" I wrote for the fun of it (
code here
).
The post got linked by Hackernews and Reddit. As is usual the majority of comments did not talk about the actual content but instead were focused on two tangential things. The first one being "this is not a full implementation of the C++ standard library as specified by the ISO standard, therefore the author is an idiot". I am, in actual fact, an idiot, but not due to project scope but because I assumed people on the Internet to have elementary reading comprehension skills. To make things clear: no, this is not an implementation of the ISO standard library. At no point was such a thing claimed. There is little point in writing one of those, there are several high quality implementations available. "Standard library" in this context means "a collection of low level functions and types that would be needed by most applications".
The second discussion was around the fact that calling the C++ standard library "STL" was both wrong and proof that the person saying that does not understand the C++ language. This was followed by several "I am a C++ standard library implementer and everyone I know calls it the STL". Things deteriorated from there.
The complexity question
Existing container implementations are complex by necessity. They need to handle things like types that can not be noexcept moved or copied. The amount of rollback code needed explodes very quickly and needs to be processed every time the header is included (because of templates). A reasonable point against writing your own containers is that eventually you need to support all the same complexity as existing ones because people will insert "bad" types into your container and complain when things fail. Thus you need to have all the same nasty, complex and brittle code as an STL implementation, only lacking decades of hardening to shake out all the bugs.
That is true, but the beauty of having zero existing users is that you can do something like this:
This is basically a concept that requires the type given to be noexcept-movable (and some other things that could arguably be removed). Now, instead of allowing any type under the sun,
all
containers require
all
types they get instantiated with to be
WellBehaved
. This means that the library
does not have to care at all
about types behaving badly because trying to use those results in a compiler error. A massive amount of complexity is thus eliminated in a single stroke.
There are of course cases when you need to deal with types that are not well behaved. If you can tolerate a memory allocation per object, the simple solution is to use
unique_ptr
. OTOH if you have types that can't be reliably moved and which are so performance critical that you can't afford memory allocations, then you are probably going to write your own container code anyway. If you are in the position that you have badly behaved types that you can't update, can't tolerate an allocation and can't write your own containers, then
that is your problem
.
Iterating things the native way
One of the most common things I do with strings in Python is to split them on whitespace. In Python this is simple as there is only one string type, but in native code things are more complicated. What should the return type of
mystring.split()
be?
vector<string>
vector<string_view>
A coroutine handle
The method should be a full template so you can customize it to output any custom string type (as every C++ code base has at least three of them)
Something ranges something something
There is probably not a single correct answer. All of the options have different tradeoffs. Thus I implemented this in two ways. The first returns a
vector<string>
as you would get in Python. The second one was a fully general, lazy and allocation-free method that uses the most unloved of language features: the void pointer.
So given that you have a callback function like this:
the split function becomes:
This is as fully general as you can get without needing to muck about with templates, coroutines or monads (I don't actually know what monads are, I'm just counting on the fact that mentioning them makes you look cool). The cost is that the end user needs to write a small adapter lambda to use it.
Iterating things the Python way
The Python iteration protocol is surprisingly simple. The object being iterated needs to provide a
.next()
method that either returns the next value or throws a
StopIteration
exception. Obviously exceptions can't be used in native code because they are too slow, but the same effect can be achieved by returning an
optional<T>
instead. Here's a unit test for an implementation of Python's
range
function.
Sadly there is not a simple way to integrate this to native loop constructs without macros and even then it is a bit ugly.
Current status
The repo has basic functionality for strings (regular and enforced UTF-8), regexes and basic containers.

data.title: Estimating Logarithms
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了John Napier提出的一种估算以10为底的对数的方法。该方法基于对数的基本性质，即一个数的对数约等于其位数减一。通过结合对数的乘法性质，可以逐步提高估算精度。例如，计算一个数的多次方，然后利用科学计数法简化计算，重复此过程可以获得更高精度。文章还提供了一个Python代码示例，展示如何通过编程实现这一算法。该方法通过不断迭代指数运算和使用科学计数法，简化了对数计算的复杂性，最终只需进行少量的乘法运算即可获得较高精度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对数的头脑估算技巧及其相关数学概念

不同观点：
• **saulpw的观点**：提出了一种简化的对数估算方法，通过将数字的位数减去1得到数量级，然后加上首位数字来进行线性插值估算。他认为这种方法适用于快速估算，并且即使有些"错误"，在粗略计算中也可以接受。
  
• **thechao的观点**：提出使用2的幂次来近似计算对数，例如通过2^10≈1024来估算log10(2)≈0.3，并使用类似的方法计算其他质数的对数。他认为掌握一些基本质数的对数值可以快速进行对数的头脑计算。

data.article_summary: "Redirector" 是一个浏览器扩展（支持Firefox、Chrome、Opera、Edge），允许用户根据正则表达式或通配符模式重定向URL，类似于客户端版的mod_rewrite。该工具可用于自动将移动网站切换为桌面版、绕过AMP页面、去除双击链接跟踪、以及将YouTube Shorts链接重定向到正常视频等。它还支持通过正则表达式处理DuckDuckGo的"!bangs"搜索快捷方式，并提供高级功能如URL解码和快速跳转到常用搜索引擎。该项目由Einar Egilsson创建和维护，以开源的MIT许可证发布，并受到广泛关注和使用。

• **重定向工具的实际应用与扩展功能**：[kmfrk] 分享了使用重定向工具的实际体验，特别是与Kagi搜索引擎结合使用的例子。他还提到了BreezeWiki项目，展示了工具在实际场景中的应用。[purpleidea] 则指出该工具缺少内置的常见修复功能，比如去除YouTube链接中的跟踪参数。

Web browser extension (Firefox, Vivaldi, Chrome, Opera, Edge) to redirect URLs based on regex or wildcard patterns.
Tribute

• **对默认设置和自动化的抱怨**：[godelski] 抱怨Wikipedia等网站在主题切换和移动端/桌面端适配上的默认设置不合理，认为这些本应自动化的功能没有做到位，增加了不必要的操作步骤。

补充讨论：
• **替代工具和解决方案**：[LargoLasskhyfv] 提到了libredirect作为一个替代工具。[altairprime] 指出Safari用户可以使用App Store中的Redirect Web工具。[snthd] 则将该工具与已停止更新的HTTPS Everywhere进行比较，认为两者功能类似。

• **安全担忧**：[amitizle] 对重定向工具可能带来的安全漏洞表示担忧，虽然没有详细说明，但这一观点提出了使用此类工具时需要注意的潜在风险。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在工具的功能完善性与安全性上，包括是否应该加入更多内置规则和如何避免重定向规则的误应用。同时，也有对网页默认设置不合理的抱怨与技术实现上的替代方案讨论。

44122860.article_content:
Clock still keeping village on time after 500 years
6 days ago
Share
Save
Joe Campbell
BBC News
Share
Save
BBC
St Augustine's clock in East Hendred has been keeping time since Henry VIII was on the throne.
Villagers have been celebrating the 500th birthday of the clock in their parish church.
The timepiece in East Hendred, near Wantage in rural Oxfordshire, is believed to be one of the oldest clocks in Britain still in its original location.
With no clock face or hands, it relies on the church bells in the tower at St Augustine's to ring out the time every quarter hour.
The decision to install it in the church was taken when Henry VIII was on the throne, explained the man responsible for St Augustine's bells, Tower Captain Nigel Findley.
"Imagine the excitement that would have caused then," he said.
The clock is linked to a carillon which uses winches and pulleys to drive hammers high above that strike the bells every quarter hour.
As well as striking the bells every quarter hour, a carillon resembling the insides of a giant musical box, plays a tune called Angel's Song four times a day, every three hours, starting at 09:00.
In 2015, one of the hammers used to strike the six bells came away and fell into the mechanism, jamming it and silencing the clock.
"It was like missing a friend," said church council secretary Ann Pappenheim. "It's a real part of living in the village.
"When you're working in the garden, it really does give you a sense of time and I missed it," she added. "Now it's back and it's wonderful."
The clock, which was originally built a few miles away in Wantage, underwent a lengthy renovation.
A modification also saw the installation of a mechanised winding system, ending the requirement for somebody to climb the narrow, winding staircase each day to the clock room to do the job by hand.
With no clock face on the tower the timepiece relies on the church bells to signal the time
This week, to mark the clock's birthday, people were able to visit the tower to see the mechanism in action.
Acting as guide was Simon Gilchrist, who led the restoration.
He described it as being "a real passion," to have spent time on the project.
"It's not often that we as clock repairers get the opportunity to work on something that is old, but also something that is of great historical importance," he said.
The clock used to be set using a sundial on the outside of the tower. Now a modern digital clock secured to the wall, next to the Tudor era mechanism is used.
"When this thing was made 500 years ago, we didn't have the accuracy that we have today," said Mr Gilchrist.
Parts of the mechanism like the pendulum expand in the summers heat and contract in the cold of winter, all affecting timekeeping.
This was a device built for a time when peoples' days began at dawn and ended shortly after the sun went down.
Given that, he added: "In terms if accuracy, it's pretty accurate."

data.title: Every 5x5 Nonogram
data.author: eieio
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要通知用户由于不活动已被断开连接，建议重新加载页面以继续游戏。同时推荐了一款新的非ogram游戏，包含超过6000个手工制作的非ogram puzzles，并且每天更新。文章还鼓励在Steam上关注"Pixelogic"游戏，并订阅每周通讯。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：5x5非ogram字谜游戏的玩法、技术实现、用户体验反馈及潜在问题

不同观点：
• okayestjoel介绍了他们开发的非ogram解谜游戏，并提到通过逻辑可以解决的5x5非ogram数量为24,976,511个。他发起了一个实时协作解谜的项目，并分享了项目的进展，已有65,000个谜题被解决。他邀请其他用户提供反馈意见。

• punty分享了一些有趣的谜题板例子，提供了具体的链接，方便其他用户直接访问这些谜题板。

• scythe表示这个游戏非常容易上瘾，自己在不知不觉中就解决了上百个谜题，暗示了游戏的吸引力。

• bspammer对游戏的可持续性表示担忧，认为有人可能会用机器人刷解谜数量，并建议通过IP限制来防止这种行为。

• 01HNNWZ0MV43FF仅提供了一个维基百科的非ogram介绍链接，未发表具体观点。

• tantalor对如何开始玩这个游戏表示困惑，询问是否需要点击某个按钮来启动谜题。

• mdtrooper分享了一个包含多种谜题的链接，未发表具体观点。

• fph提到了可能存在的敏感内容（swastika picture），提醒大家注意。

• Waterluvian讨论了5x5非ogram不需要猜测即可通过逻辑解决的特点，并建议可能有相关的数学视频解释这一现象。随后，Waterluvian再次反馈UI设计问题，特别是如何找到未完成的谜题。

• anxiousbuddhist表示非常喜欢这个游戏，并建议增加隐藏已完成和进行中谜题的功能，以提升用户体验。

• NooneAtAll3提到页面重置问题，导致无法从中间开始解谜，影响了游戏体验。

• manarth提到服务器通信问题频繁出现，猜测可能是由于机器人活动或HN hug of death导致的。

• x-complexity从技术角度讨论了如何将解谜结果编码为整数，并提出了使用非ogram进行信息混淆的可能性。

• butz回忆了自己年轻时的一个类似项目，并考虑将其扩展到更高 bit 颜色的像素图标。

补充讨论：
• 游戏的吸引力及上瘾性被scythe和okayestjoel强调，但也有用户如Waterluvian和NooneAtAll3提出了用户体验方面的问题。
• 技术实现和潜在问题如bspammer提到的机器人问题、manarth遇到的服务器问题也被讨论，显示出用户对游戏可持续性和技术稳定性的关注。
• 争议的焦点在于用户体验和游戏功能上的不足，特别是如何找到未完成的谜题和页面重置问题。

Frequently Asked Questions
What is PlayDiffusion?
PlayDiffusion is an advanced AI voice model that uses diffusion-based technology for natural speech editing and inpainting. It enables precise modifications of audio segments while maintaining context and speaker characteristics.
How does PlayDiffusion work?
PlayDiffusion uses a novel diffusion-based approach that encodes audio into discrete tokens, masks the target segment, and employs a diffusion model to denoise the masked region while preserving surrounding context. The result is then transformed back to speech using our BigVGAN decoder.
What makes PlayDiffusion different from other voice models?
PlayDiffusion's key differentiators include its non-autoregressive architecture (up to 50x faster generation), seamless context preservation, and advanced speaker conditioning. Unlike traditional models, it can edit portions of audio without discontinuity artifacts.
Where can I try PlayDiffusion?
You can experience PlayDiffusion through Play Studio or access the source code and model weights on Hugging Face. The model is open-source and available for researchers and developers.
What are the main applications of PlayDiffusion?
PlayDiffusion excels in voice editing, speech inpainting, and text-to-speech applications. It's particularly effective for modifying specific segments of audio while maintaining natural transitions and speaker consistency.
Is PlayDiffusion suitable for real-time applications?
Yes, PlayDiffusion's efficient non-autoregressive architecture makes it suitable for real-time applications. Its optimized token generation process significantly reduces computational requirements while maintaining high quality.

In this article
Actionable Intelligence to Improve How the Ably Team Works
Looking Ahead
Key Learnings

Jamie Newcomb
is Head of Product Ops and Delivery at Ably.
Editor’s Note:
Jellyfish launched the
Jellyfish MCP server
this April to allow LLMs to access Jellyfish data via our API. Jellyfish customers can now seamlessly integrate any data accessible via the Jellyfish API into their AI-powered workflows, chatbots and agents. This article illustrates how it’s already helping organizations like Able more readily access their data.
When Jellyfish launched their MCP this April, I primarily used it as an exploratory tool, but the potential quickly became clear. My initial hypothesis was that this could make Jellyfish data more accessible to team members who don’t spend much time in the platform itself.
Instead of requiring everyone to navigate dashboards and filters, I could ask natural language questions like:
“What are our current investment levels for May?”
“Which outcomes/deliverables are being targeted for May?”
“How much did we invest in the Chat moderation outcomes in May?”
These initial prompts were answered well, providing clear responses that demonstrated the potential of this approach. And while I haven’t rolled this out to others yet, I can already see how this approach could break down barriers for team members who need insights but aren’t regular Jellyfish users.
Actionable Intelligence to Improve How the Ably Team Works
Actionable Intelligence to Improve How the Ably Team Works
The real power emerged when I moved beyond simple data retrieval to analysis and insights. When I asked, “How is developer productivity in the xyz team this month?” Something awesome happened.
The AI didn’t just return raw metrics. Instead, it:
Intelligently identified all key metrics associated with developer productivity
Analysed the data to understand potential reasons for performance patterns
Connected insights across different Jellyfish data points, linking productivity metrics to investment levels and deliverable timelines
Most impressively, it concluded that productivity appeared lower because the team was split across multiple investment categories and several outcomes had just kicked off. This matched our internal hypothesis perfectly, but the AI had arrived at this conclusion independently by analysing the data relationships in seconds.
I then tested more specific queries, asking “How does PR cycle time compare within the xyz team for April?” The results went far beyond a simple data dump:
Individual PR cycle times were listed for each team member
The AI provided contextual explanations for why each person’s metrics might look the way they did
It identified patterns, noting that certain team members had higher PR review counts
Most remarkably, it correctly inferred these were likely tech leads carrying a heavier review burden
This wasn’t just showing data, it was providing actionable intelligence that could be used to improve processes and ways of working.
The true potential became apparent when I connected additional MCP servers alongside Jellyfish. Within minutes, we could:
Ask Claude for insights from Jellyfish data about team performance
Have it analyse our documented processes in Confluence to identify potential inefficiencies
Receive specific suggestions for process improvements based on the gap between documented intent and measured reality
This connected workflow happened seamlessly in a single conversation. We moved from “What does our data show?” to “How can we improve based on what we know?” in real-time.
Looking Ahead
Looking Ahead
We’re working toward connecting more data sources and potentially making this accessible to more people through remote MCP servers. I see this development as a powerful complement to traditional dashboards, offering a more conversational way to interact with the rich data that Jellyfish provides – creating an additional interface that can make Jellyfish insights more accessible to different types of users and use cases.
Having data accessible through one UI where you can ask exactly what you want and get additional insights represents a substantial productivity and efficiency gain. The advantages are clear:
Single conversational interface alongside existing dashboards
Natural language queries for users who prefer this interaction style
Contextual insights generated automatically
Connected analysis across previously siloed systems
When your LLM understands how you set out to work (documented processes), how you’re actually working (Jellyfish metrics), and the impact on your goals (outcomes data), it becomes a powerful tool for identifying workflow inefficiencies and optimisation opportunities.

I began with basic data access questions and let the use cases evolve naturally.

data.author: neocanable
data.article_summary: "Garlic" 是一个用C语言编写的Java反编译工具，能够从 `.class`、`.jar` 和 `.war` 文件生成Java源代码。它具有多线程支持，并且比 `javap` 更快。项目使用 `cmake` 构建，没有其他依赖项。基本用法包括指定文件路径进行反编译，默认输出到控制台，也可通过 `-o` 选项指定输出路径。`-t` 选项可设置线程数，默认是4。该工具目前不支持 `.dex` 文件反编译。项目遵循Apache-2.0许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源项目的许可证兼容性、内存管理问题、与其他类似工具的比较及未来计划、使用C语言开发新项目的合理性、以及对项目动机的询问。

不同观点：
• **许可证问题**：[kazinator] 指出项目中使用了GPL2许可证下的代码（hashmap.c），而项目本身是基于Apache 2.0许可证，这可能导致许可证不兼容的问题。

• **内存管理问题**：[gibibit] 关注项目中的内存管理，尤其是`string class_simple_name(string full)`函数中静态字符串和堆分配字符串的混用问题。这种做法会导致调用者无法正确释放内存，可能引发内存泄漏。

• **工具比较与建议**：
  ◦ [jbellis] 提到FernFlower反编译器，认为它是IntelliJ中的标准工具，并指出JBoss也有一个FernFlower反编译库，可能对项目有参考价值。
  ◦ [stefanos82] 推荐了JD-GUI工具，认为其作为Java反编译器可能对项目有帮助。

• **未来功能建议**：
  ◦ [appendixv3] 对项目的速度表示赞赏，并询问未来是否计划支持`.dex`文件以及如何处理JAR中的内部类。

• **工具效果比较**：[cosmolev] 询问该项目输出结果与https://www.decompiler.com/在正确性方面的比较。

• **使用C语言开发新项目的合理性**：[kamma4434] 质疑在2025年使用C语言开始新项目的合理性，将其比喻为“驾驶没有安全带的汽车”，暗示C语言在安全性和开发效率上的不足。

• **项目动机与技术选择**：
  ◦ [keepamovin] 对项目是通过人工还是AI完成表示好奇，并询问项目的动机。
  ◦ [ConanRus] 则提出是否可以编写一个纯Java语言的C语言反编译器，质疑项目技术选择的合理性。

补充讨论：
• 许可证兼容性问题可能是争议的焦点，因为这涉及到法律合规和代码使用权限。
• 内存管理问题则是技术上的一个重要关注点，直接影响项目的稳定性和可靠性。
• 对未来功能和实现方式的建议反映了社区对项目扩展性和实用性的期望。
• 使用C语言开发新项目的合理性以及技术选择问题引发了对项目长期可维护性和开发难度的讨论。

44169132.article_summary: "Garlic" 是一个用C语言编写的Java反编译工具，能够从 `.class`、`.jar` 和 `.war` 文件生成Java源代码。它具有多线程支持，并且比 `javap` 更快。项目使用 `cmake` 构建，没有其他依赖项。基本用法包括指定文件路径进行反编译，默认输出到控制台，也可通过 `-o` 选项指定输出路径。`-t` 选项可设置线程数，默认是4。该工具目前不支持 `.dex` 文件反编译。项目遵循Apache-2.0许可证。

data.title: Covert Web-to-App Tracking via Localhost on Android
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文披露了一种影响数亿Android用户的新型跟踪方法，涉及Meta和Yandex。这些公司通过其Android应用（如Facebook、Instagram、Yandex Maps和Browser）在设备本地端口上监听，以获取用户浏览器的元数据、 cookies和指令。具体来说，Meta的Pixel和Yandex的Metrica脚本在网页上加载，并通过localhost套接字与设备上的原生应用通信，分享标识符和浏览习惯。这种方法绕过了隐私保护措施，如清除cookies、隐身模式和Android的权限控制，甚至可能被恶意应用利用来窃听用户网络活动。

Meta的Pixel脚本通过WebRTC将_fbp cookie传输到其Android应用，这些应用在后台监听特定端口。尽管在披露后Meta停止了这种行为，但该方法曾成功将用户的网页浏览与应用账户关联，从而去匿名化用户。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta Pixel等技术滥用及其安全问题，以及跨平台和跨应用的跟踪和数据泄露风险

不同观点：
• **neilv**：认为Google等公司知道ID滥用的可能性，并应制定规则防止滥用，比如Play Store永久封禁、法律诉讼等。但像Meta这样的科技巨头可能难以被处罚。同时，某些技术滥用可能与情报机构或执法部门有关，使得问题更加复杂。
• **bravesoul2**：关注跨用户配置文件的数据交换问题，指出如果个人配置文件中的受感染应用可以与另一个配置文件中的网站交换数据，将带来严重的安全隐患。
• **dylan604**：讨论Meta Pixel脚本的端口监听行为，指出某些端口被监听但未被使用，推测可能是应用逐步推出的结果，并提出是否可以伪造消息发送到这些端口的问题。
• **bnpxft**：建议避免安装大科技公司的应用，仅使用其网站，因为网站受限于浏览器沙盒，相对更安全。
• **chedabob**：质疑Yandex是否在应用中附带了其证书的私钥，从而允许本地网络中的其他设备伪造Yandex Metrica网站。
• **josephcsible**：建议所有浏览器阻止对localhost的跨源访问，以防止潜在的安全风险。
• **matthberg**：指出浏览器允许网页访问局域网资源是一个仍未被很好解决的攻击向量，并提到uBlock Origin和Port Authority等工具可以用于阻止此类访问，但仍可能存在绕过机制。
• **jeroenhd**：认为浏览器允许STUN/TURN到localhost是一个明显的攻击机制，并建议开发一个通知用户的应用，当UDP流量进入时发出警告。同时，提出是否可以通过为每个应用分配不同的IPv6地址来防止此类跟踪。
• **fsflover**：提供了一个相关讨论的链接，暗示对类似问题的讨论在其他地方也存在。
• **maeil**：提到欧盟对美国科技公司的罚款问题，认为如果科技公司停止这些不当行为，将不会被罚款。
• **lachlan_gray**：询问iOS上是否存在类似的问题，特别是当应用请求“查找我的网络设备”时。
• **hofrogs**：认为Meta等公司应受到法律制裁，但预计实际上不会发生任何事情。
• **worik**：建议尽量少安装应用，以减少潜在的安全风险。
• **captn3m0**：指出另一个类似的跟踪向量，即通过android.intent.action.MAIN查询所有安装的应用，而无需QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES权限，且Google未对此做出回应。
• **JimDabell**：提供了一个关于阻止此类行为的规范链接，并指出该规范曾获得WebKit和Mozilla的支持，但在Blink中由于兼容性问题被搁置。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到浏览器和应用的安全漏洞以及可能的解决方案，例如阻止跨源访问localhost、分配不同的IPv6地址等。
• 对Meta和其他大科技公司滥用技术的批评，以及对监管机构不作为的质疑，是另一个值得注意的讨论点。
• 技术细节如端口监听、证书伪造、跨配置文件数据交换等，展示了问题的复杂性和多样性。

44169314.article_content:
Disclosure: Covert Web-to-App Tracking via
Localhost on Android
We disclose a novel tracking method by Meta and Yandex potentially affecting
billions of Android users. We found that native Android apps—including
Facebook,
Instagram
, and
several
Yandex apps including Maps and Browser—silently listen on fixed local
ports
for tracking purposes.
These native Android apps receive browsers' metadata, cookies and commands from
the Meta Pixel and Yandex Metrica scripts embedded on thousands of web sites. These JavaScripts load
on users' mobile browsers and silently connect with native apps running on the same device through
localhost sockets. As native apps access programatically
device identifiers like the
Android
Advertising ID (AAID)
or handle user identities as in the case
of Meta apps, this method effectively allows these organizations to
link mobile
browsing sessions and web cookies to user identities
, hence de-anonymizing users'
visiting sites embedding their scripts.
This web-to-app ID sharing method bypasses typical privacy protections such as clearing
cookies, Incognito Mode and Android's permission controls. Worse, it opens the door for potentially
malicious apps eavesdropping on users’ web activity.
📢
UPDATE
: As of June 3rd 7:45 CEST, Meta/Facebook Pixel script is no longer
sending
any packets or requests to localhost. The code responsible for sending the _fbp cookie has been
almost
completely removed.
How does this work?
While there are subtle differences in the way Meta and Yandex bridge web and mobile
contexts and identifiers, both of them essentially misuse the unvetted access to localhost
sockets.
The Android OS allows any installed app with the INTERNET permission to open a
listening socket on the loopback interface (127.0.0.1). Browsers running on the same
device also access this interface without user consent or platform mediation. This
allows JavaScript embedded on web pages to communicate with native Android apps and
share identifiers and browsing habits
, bridging ephemeral web identifiers
to long-lived mobile app IDs using standard Web APIs.
Meta/Facebook Pixel sharing _fbp cookie from web to Meta Android apps
The Meta (Facebook) Pixel JavaScript, when loaded in an Android mobile web browser,
transmits
the first-party
_fbp
cookie using WebRTC to UDP ports 12580–12585 to
any app on the device that is listening on those ports. We found Meta-owned Android apps
Facebook
(version 515.0.0.23.90) and Instagram
(version 382.0.0.43.84), available on the Google Play Store, listening on these port range.
As of 25 2025, the Meta Pixel uses a technique known as
SDP Munging
to insert
the
_fbp
cookie contents to the SDP "ice-ufrag" field, resulting in a
Binding Request STUN message sent to the loopback address as the following figure shows.
This data flow cannot be observed using Chrome's regular debugging tools (such as DevTools).
The entire flow of the _fbp cookie from web to native and the server is as follows:
The user opens the native Facebook or Instagram app, which eventually is sent to the
background and creates
a background service to listen for incoming traffic on a TCP port (12387 or 12388)
and a UDP port (the first unoccupied port in 12580-12585). Users must be logged-in with
their credentials on the apps.
The user opens their browser and visits a website integrating the Meta Pixel.
At this stage, websites may ask for consent depending on the website's and visitor's
locations.
).
The Meta Pixel script sends the
_fbp cookie
to the native Instagram or Facebook app via WebRTC (STUN) SDP Munging.
The Meta Pixel script also sends the _fbp value in a request to
https://www.facebook.com/tr
along with other parameters such as page URL (dl), website and browser metadata, and the
event
type
(ev) (e.g., PageView, AddToCart, Donate, Purchase).
The Facebook or Instagram apps receive the _fbp cookie from the Meta Pixel JavaScript
running
on the
browser. The apps transmit _fbp as a GraphQL mutation to
(https://graph[.]facebook[.]com/graphql) along with other persistent user identifiers,
linking users' fbp ID (web visit) with their Facebook or Instagram account.
On or around May 17th, Meta Pixel added a new method to their script that sends the _fbp cookie
using
WebRTC TURN
instead
of STUN. The new TURN method avoids SDP Munging, which Chrome developers publicly announced
to disable following our disclosure. As of June 2, 2025, we have not observed the Facebook
or Instagram applications actively listening on these new ports.
About the _fbp cookie
According to Meta’s Cookies Policy, the
_fbp
cookie
identifies browsers for the purposes of providing advertising and site analytics
services and has a lifespan of 90 days
.
The cookie is present on approximately 25% of the top million websites, making it the 3rd
most common
first-party cookie of the web,
according
to Web Almanac 2024
.
A first-party cookie implies that it cannot be used to track users across websites, as it is
set under the website’s domain.

data.title: Mario Kart designers had to rethink everything to make it open world
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 《Mario Kart World》作为Nintendo Switch 2的首发游戏，对系列进行了重大变革。游戏设计师旨在将参赛者数量翻倍，并打造一个开放世界，供玩家自由探索。由于原Switch硬件无法满足需求，开发转至性能更强的Switch 2。制作人Kosuke Yabuki表示，这个开放世界并非基于现实地点设计，而是纯粹为了提升游戏乐趣。世界各元素相互关联，地形设计的改动会影响整体，使得赛道设计更加复杂。新作引入全新模式“Knockout Tour”，玩家在整个大陆上竞速，人数逐渐减少。此外，关于Toad的头部装饰，Yabuki暗示其中秘密，鼓励玩家自行探索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对即将推出的开放世界《Mario Kart》的看法和争议

不同观点：
• **期待与好奇**：
  - [bee_rider] 对开放世界《Mario Kart》感到好奇，认为这种设计可能有趣，但也提到了《Pokemon》开放世界游戏表现不佳的例子，表达了对是否能成功的怀疑。
  - [Jyaif] 表示对游戏的期待，认为它可能满足自己对开放世界和物理引擎结合的游戏需求。

• **对赛道设计的担忧**：
  - [dragontamer] 担心长直道的设计会削弱《Mario Kart》原有的策略性，特别是漂移和过弯的乐趣，但对游戏的其他改进表示认可，认为这种大胆的设计需要时间验证。
  - [bigstrat2003] 对增加到24个赛车手的设计不满，也不喜欢开放世界的概念，认为这会使游戏不如以前的版本有趣。

• **对价格的批评**：
  - [ThatMedicIsASpy] 表示不愿意为没有实体周边（如手册或雕像）的游戏花费超过80美元，提到了《Need for Speed Underground》从线性转变为开放世界时的失败。
  - [jsheard] 同样对价格上涨表示不满，尤其是考虑到未来可能还会推出付费DLC，并对《Switch 2》整个生命周期中价格不会下降表示担忧。

• **与其他游戏的比较**：
  - [jeron] 认为开放世界赛车游戏并不新颖，提到了《The Crew》和《Forza Horizon》系列，暗示任天堂可能只是借鉴了其他成功的开放世界游戏设计。
  - [rhodey] 提到了《Kirby Air Ride》，认为新《Mario Kart》可能与该游戏有相似之处。

• **对游戏细节的幽默评论**：
  - [treetalker] 以幽默的方式讨论了游戏中Toad角色的设计，认为这是游戏中最重要且神秘的元素，提出了有趣的哲学问题。

• **对设计理念的质疑**：
  - [AllegedAlec] 引用了著名电影台词，质疑游戏设计者是否过于专注于能否实现开放世界，而忽略了是否应该这样做。

补充讨论：
- 总体来看，玩家对于开放世界《Mario Kart》的态度存在明显分歧，一部分人表示期待和好奇，另一部分人则对赛道设计、价格和游戏理念提出质疑和批评。争议的焦点在于开放世界设计是否适合《Mario Kart》系列，以及长直道对游戏策略性的影响。价格问题也是讨论的一个重要方面，特别是与游戏内容和附加DLC相关的问题。

44170708.article_content:
Report
/
Interview
Mario Kart World’s designers had to rethink everything to make it open world
Producer Kosuke Yabuki talks about what went into building the Nintendo Switch 2 launch title.
by
Andrew Webster
Jun 3, 2025, 2:00 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Image: Nintendo
Andrew Webster
is an entertainment editor covering streaming, virtual worlds, and every single Pokémon video game. Andrew joined The Verge in 2012, writing over 4,000 stories.
From the very beginning, the goal for
Mario Kart World
was ambitious. A follow-up to the Switch’s (and Wii U’s) best-selling game,
one that steadily grew over the years
,
World
’s original concept focused on two key changes: doubling the amount of racers, and creating a connected, open world for players to explore. It was so big that, early on in development for the original Switch, the team was having a hard time making it work on the hardware, and eventually it shifted to become the main launch title for the more powerful Switch 2.
But even outside of technical issues, those changes meant a fundamental rethink of many of
Mario Kart
’s core elements. “We knew when we came up with this idea that it really would be a big change for the series,” says producer Kosuke Yabuki, “but we had no idea at the time how many people, how much time, and how much effort that would require to actually achieve it.”
The most obvious change is right there in the title: it’s the world. Instead of a series of individual racetracks, all of
Mario Kart World
’s courses take place on the same landmass, connected by a series of routes. The game isn’t set in an existing version of the Mushroom Kingdom, but instead a brand-new location that has been designed from the ground-up around the idea of racing.
“As you travel through this world, you will see things that remind you of the Mushroom Kingdom,” Yabuki explains. “Elements like the question mark blocks or warp pipes. In terms of world design, I would say this world was designed for
Mario Kart World
. If you look at the height of a mountain, or the length of a desert, those were all things that we decided specifically for this title.”
According to Yabuki – who previously worked on both
Mario Kart 7
and
8
, and served as producer on
the Switch fighter
Arms
– unlike many open worlds, the game wasn’t designed to be a recreation of a realistic or believable place. He says that “we have to think about not simply recreating real-world patterns in terms of a town or an island. Rather, this world exists purely to make
Mario Kart
more fun.”
Image: Nintendo
Building the world wasn’t difficult purely because it was larger than past games, but also because of that connected nature. As Yabuki explains it, when one element of the world was changed, it had a cascading effect that could impact other parts of the world as well. “If you change the height of a mountain you have to think about whether you’ve diminished its usefulness in the surrounding areas as a landmark, for example,” Yabuki says. “This means that in the end terrain design is actually quite a difficult task, because if you change one thing, you have to adjust many more.”
This influenced the way the race tracks themselves were designed. In previous
Mario Kart
games, the developers had more control over how players were able to view the courses, because they were racing along pre-defined roads and paths. But that’s no longer the case.
“You used to be designing courses with the notion that people are going to drive and look in a very few fixed directions that we know ahead of time,” Yabuki says, “compared to
Mario Kart World
, where people might enter a course from anywhere, or leave that course from anywhere, and continue driving. So we have to think about those entry and exit points, and how they affect the player’s vantage. In that sense,
Mario Kart World
course design is quite a bit more work compared to previous games.”
What is on Toad’s head?
In 2018,
Super Mario Odyssey
producer Yoshiaki Koizumi
confirmed a long-debated fact: the mushroom on Toad’s head is actually his head, and not a hat. But Toad’s appearance in
Mario Kart World
, in which he’s wearing a racing helmet, raises a new question as to what the helmet actually is. Unfortunately,
like in some of my past Mario-related investigations
, I was unable to get a definitive answer on this.
“When it comes to Toad, there really are a lot of secrets about this character, and I have to say not all of them are mine to share,” Yabuki told me. “But I would like for you, when you play the game, to consider when Toad is wearing a helmet, sometimes he’ll have that transform and you’ll see suddenly it’s a hamburger. So I want you to think about that moment and what your personal theory about Toad’s head might be.”
The expansiveness similarly had an impact on the game’s structure. For one thing, it inspired an all-new mode called Knockout Tour, where players are racing across the entire continent, while their numbers steadily dwindle, sort of like a
44170708.article_summary: 《Mario Kart World》作为Nintendo Switch 2的首发游戏，对系列进行了重大变革。游戏设计师旨在将参赛者数量翻倍，并打造一个开放世界，供玩家自由探索。由于原Switch硬件无法满足需求，开发转至性能更强的Switch 2。制作人Kosuke Yabuki表示，这个开放世界并非基于现实地点设计，而是纯粹为了提升游戏乐趣。世界各元素相互关联，地形设计的改动会影响整体，使得赛道设计更加复杂。新作引入全新模式“Knockout Tour”，玩家在整个大陆上竞速，人数逐渐减少。此外，关于Toad的头部装饰，Yabuki暗示其中秘密，鼓励玩家自行探索。

data.title: Illicit crypto-miners pouncing on lazy DevOps configs leaving clouds vulnerable
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 文章主要报道了一个名为JINX-0132的黑客团伙，利用云环境中DevOps工具的错误配置进行非法加密货币挖矿活动。该团伙主要针对HashiCorp的Nomad和Consul工具、Docker API以及Gitea等应用。Wiz的研究显示，约25%的云用户可能受到影响，其中5%直接将这些工具暴露在互联网中，30%存在配置错误。JINX-0132通过利用这些漏洞部署XMRig挖矿软件。为防止此类攻击，建议用户启用Nomad和Consul的安全功能，如访问控制列表，并避免将Docker API暴露在互联网中。Gitea方面，攻击者可能利用旧版本的漏洞（如CVE-2020-14144）进行攻击，因此及时更新和配置安全设置至关重要。

不同观点：
• **[latchkey]** 认为，将问题归咎于加密货币矿工是一种常见的刻板印象。他指出，由于以太坊（ETH）从工作量证明（PoW）转向权益证明（PoS），CPU/GPU挖矿已经不再有利可图，整个挖矿行业受到了重创。除了少数深度参与者还能赚取一些收入外，挖矿无法再推动整个市场。

• **[gavinray]** 分享了个人经历，他的AWS账户遭到入侵，攻击者利用他的安全密钥启动了多个EC2实例进行加密货币挖矿，导致他收到了600美元的账单。他批评AWS缺乏自动化的大规模服务清理工具，最终他的账户被永久关闭。他从中吸取了教训，强调在绑定信用卡的在线服务上必须启用双因素认证（2-FA）。

• **[udev4096]** 强调了运行任何服务时都不应盲目暴露在互联网上，至少应设置身份验证。他认为在一些自我托管和家庭实验室的社区中，安全实践比一些公司更为严谨。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：是否应将问题归咎于矿工以及当前加密货币挖矿是否仍然有利可图。
• **实际案例**：[gavinray]的真实案例展示了云服务账户被滥用于挖矿的问题，以及在处理这种问题时云服务提供商的不足之处。
• **安全建议**：强调了双因素认证（2-FA）在保护在线账户方面的重要性以及服务暴露在互联网上时的基本安全措施。

Security
1
Illicit crypto-miners pouncing on lazy DevOps configs that leave clouds vulnerable
1
To stop the JINX-0132 gang behind these attacks, pay attention to HashiCorp, Docker, and Gitea security settings
Jessica Lyons
Tue 3 Jun 2025
//
11:23 UTC
Up to a quarter of all cloud users are at risk of having their computing resources stolen and used to illicitly mine for cryptocurrency, after crims cooked up a campaign that targets publicly accessible DevOps tools.
Wiz Threat Research spotted the campaign and attributed it to an attacker it named JINX–0132, which it says exploits misconfigurations and vulnerabilities in multiple applications to deploy mining software.
JINX–0132 targets a "wide range" of DevOps tools, but Wiz thinks it prefers HashiCorp’s Nomad and Consul tools, plus Docker API and Gitea.
According to threat researchers Gili Tikochinski, Danielle Aminov and Merav Bar, Wiz data indicates that 25 percent of all cloud environments are running at least one of these technologies, and more than 20 percent run HashiCorp Consul.
We've asked the Wiz kids how many instances of those applications JINX–0132 hit and will update this story when we hear back from the
soon-to-be-Google-owned
security shop.
"Of those environments using these DevOps tools, five percent expose them directly to the Internet, and among those exposed deployments, 30 percent are misconfigured," the team
wrote
.
Here's a look at the four under–fire tools, and the flaws in each that Wiz says JINX–0132 is looking to abuse.
HashiCorp Nomad
Nomad is a scheduler and orchestrator used to deploy containers and applications across multiple platforms. According to HashiCorp's
documentation
, Nomad is not secure by default.
For example, default settings in the software’s job queue feature, which schedules and manages jobs, allow any user with access to the Nomad server API to create and run such jobs.
HashiCorp suggests users take several steps to address that.
Therein lies the problem, according to Wiz, because JINX–0132 found a publicly exposed Nomad server – Shodan scans can find 405 of them – running out–of–the–box settings without security features enabled.
JINX–0132 used that insecure server to download and run XMRig miner software.
To ensure this doesn't happen to you, turn on Nomad features documented in HashiCorp’s
Security Model
section and make sure access control lists deny unauthorized access to the Jobs feature.
HashiCorp Consul
The second HashiCorp tool JINX–0132 abused in this campaign is Consul, a networking platform that manages network connectivity between services and across on–premises and multi–cloud environments.
Fresh Consul installations do not populate access control lists or enable other security features by default.
'Ongoing' Ivanti hijack bug exploitation reaches clouds
Public–facing Kubernetes clusters at risk of takeover thanks to Ingress–Nginx flaw
Google acquisition target Wiz links fresh supply chain attack to 23K pwned GitHub repos
Cryptojacking, backdoors abound as fiends abuse Aviatrix Controller bug
HashiCorp has
warned for years
that attackers can use such configurations to achieve remote code execution. And this is what JINX–0132 did, abusing this feature to add malicious checks that execute miners.
"Much like their procedure for hijacking Nomad, JINX–0132 adds multiple services with seemingly random names whose real purpose was to download and run the XMRig payload," the Wiz trio wrote.
Keep JINX–0132 off your cloud computing resources by implementing security documented
here
, such as disabling script checks by setting the "enable–script–checks" flag to "false," and restrict the HTTP API to only bind only to "localhost" wherever possible.
Docker Engine API
Wiz has previously documented several instances of
misconfigurations
that expose Docker APIs to the public internet. Those errors give attackers the same access as the root–owned Docker command–line–interface and allow remote code execution.
As Tikochinski, Aminov, and Bar wrote:
Attackers can create a container that mounts the host filesystem – POST to /containers/create with "Binds":["/:/host"], then POST to /containers/{id}/start, or launch a crypto–miner image by POSTing to /containers/create, POSTing to /containers/{id}/start, or dropping straight into an interactive shell via /exec.
Attackers can also use this illicit access to control Docker from within a container, then pivoting to Kubernetes or other hosts, we're told.
"Simply not exposing the API to the Internet is the most effective mitigation," the Wiz team said.
Gitea
Wiz’s researchers are not sure how JINX–0132 gains access to Gitea, but the team details several possibilities in its research.
Two of them – exploiting an insecure default vulnerability (
CVE–2020–14144
) in older versions and manually changing the default secure settings in Version 1.13 to allow users to create custom Git Hooks – require authentication to be exploited. Therefore, exploiting both CVEs for RCE isn’t realist

data.title: Show HN: Kan.bn – An open-source alterative to Trello
data.author: henryball
data.article_summary: Kan是一款开源的Trello替代品，用于项目管理。它提供板可见性控制、团队成员邀请、Trello板导入、标签与过滤、评论、活动日志等功能，并计划推出模板和集成工具。技术上使用Next.js、tRPC、Tailwind CSS、Drizzle ORM等。项目遵循AGPL-3.0许可证，欢迎贡献，并提供详细的开发设置指南和环境变量说明。如需支持，可联系团队或加入Discord服务器。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源Trello替代品 KanBN 的功能、技术选型、竞争优势及未来发展方向

不同观点：
• [henryball] 介绍了自己开发的 KanBN 项目，强调其速度快、免费、可完全自定义，并且支持自托管或使用云版本。他欢迎反馈和功能建议。
• [SwiftyBug] 质疑选择 Next.js 作为开源项目技术栈，认为该技术在非 Vercel 环境下的部署非常困难。
• [remram] 对项目标语 "Kanban reimagined" 提出异议，认为其功能与 Trello 及其他类似工具并无显著区别，称不上是“重新想象”。
• [AnonC] 建议增加家庭计划和原生应用支持，尤其是 iCloud 或 Dropbox 同步功能，并表达了对订阅制的不满。
• [wood_spirit] 希望有一个开源的“全能”应用，能够整合 Slack、Kanban、HTTP 机器人、图表和 Python 笔记本等功能。
• [subpixel] 提到 Trello 的价格已经下调至 $5/月，新项目很难在价格上竞争，除非有像条件自动化这样的独特功能。
• [mdtrooper] 提到多年前使用的 Kanboard 也是一个不错的开源选择，虽然界面丑陋但功能实用且易于安装。
• [aarreedd] 建议构建一个专门运行在 Cloudflare Workers 上的类似应用，可以实现基本免费、简单访问控制、易于自托管和 AI 集成等功能。
• [voldrix] 分享了自己制作的简易 Trello 克隆版，但仅支持单用户且无认证功能。
• [column] 提供用户体验反馈，指出在创建工作区、看板或列表时，按下 "Enter" 键与点击 "Create" 按钮效果不同，并建议提供更清晰的界面解释。
• [ramoz] 感谢其他用户推荐的 Kanboard，并分享了其安装步骤。
• [singiamtel] 对项目的域名提出质疑。
• [appendixv2] 对项目使用的技术栈表示赞赏，并询问是否计划支持自托管邮件选项如 SMTP 或 Mailgun。
• [yolkedgeek] 批评继续使用 React 和 Next.js 构建新项目的做法，认为这导致了大量 Trello 替代品的存在。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：KanBN 是否真正“重新想象”了 Kanban，以及 Next.js 技术栈在开源项目中的适用性。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：项目的定价策略、自托管和原生应用的需求、与其他开源工具（如 Kanboard）的比较、技术实现（如 Cloudflare Workers 和邮件选项）的可行性。

data.title: What Is "Seeing" in Astrophotography? The Science Behind Atmospheric Turbulence
data.author: karlperera
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了天文摄影中“视宁度”（seeing）的概念及其重要性。视宁度指地球大气层的稳定性和质量，它影响通过望远镜观测或拍摄的天体清晰度。大气湍流导致光线不规则折射，使星星闪烁，图像模糊。即使是专业观测站，视宁度通常也在0.5到1.5角秒之间，而业余天文爱好者的观测点通常为2到4角秒。这意味着无论望远镜多大，大气湍流通常限制了照片的清晰度。

视宁度对行星摄影影响最大，因为需要高分辨率捕捉细节。文章提供了测量和应对不良视宁度的工具和技巧，例如使用山顶或太空望远镜减少大气干扰。此外，还区分了视宁度与透明度（大气清澈度）的不同。最后，文章建议在不良视宁度下如何尽量改善拍摄结果，强调适应环境的重要性。

参考链接提供了进一步的教程和资源。

不同观点：

Astronomy Basics
What does seeing mean in astrophotography?
Posted by
Karl Perera MA
–
May 28, 2025
Table of Contents
What is Astronomical Seeing?
How Does Seeing Affect Your Images?
My First Experience with Bad Seeing
How to Measure Seeing Conditions
When is Seeing at Its Best?
Tools to Check Seeing Conditions
Tips for Dealing with Poor Seeing
Seeing vs Transparency: What’s the Difference?
How to Improve Your Results Despite Poor Seeing
Conclusion: Working with What You’ve Got
References
The night sky was crystal clear, stars shimmering gently. I had my
telescope perfectly aligned
,
camera settings
optimized, and target acquired—Jupiter, in all its glory. But when I reviewed my images later, instead of the sharp, detailed gas giant I expected, I found only a blurry, wobbling mess. What went wrong? The culprit wasn’t my equipment or technique—it was something far more fundamental that many beginning astrophotographers overlook: atmospheric seeing conditions. Understanding this single factor could be the difference between frustrating failures and breathtaking cosmic portraits. Here’s what five years of stargazing have taught me about working with (and sometimes against) our turbulent atmosphere.
To understand why my Jupiter photos failed that night, we first need to answer this question: what does seeing mean in astrophotography?
What is Astronomical Seeing?
Astronomical seeing refers to the quality and stability of Earth’s atmosphere and how it affects the sharpness of celestial objects when viewed or photographed through a telescope. Poor seeing makes stars appear to twinkle and blurs objects, while good seeing allows for sharp, steady views.
While this definition explains the basics, the reality of how our atmosphere interferes with starlight is far more complex than most people realize.
Diagram showing how disturbances in the atmosphere affect astronomical images
Let’s look more closely at how Earth’s atmosphere affects how we see objects in space from the ground. Most people think of air as empty space, but that is far from the truth. If this were true, then aeroplanes wouldn’t fly. In fact, the way a plane flies is similar to a surfer riding the waves. Yes, air can be thought of as being like water in that it moves about and changing constantly. Some areas are warmer or cooler, and some areas can be very disturbed, with changes in the direction and speed of movement similar to waves in water.
Atmospheric seeing changes according to the conditions in the air. Imagine taking a photo through water in a swimming pool. One moment the view of the bottom is clear and the next it isn’t because the water is moving and the light moves and bends in different ways. In the sky this movement and change in the air causes stars to flicker and twinkle. If you look at the moon through a telescope you can see the surface moving about almost as if you are looking through water. It’s never still because there is so much atmosphere between us and space.
What’s the technical explanation? Seeing is caused by turbulent pockets of air with different temperatures and densities that bend light irregularly as it passes through. This causes blurry images and distortions in what we see. The images are less sharp than if we were viewing them from outside the atmosphere in space. This is why we have telescopes high up at the tops of mountains or out in space where there is less disturbance from the air above us.
In fact, the impact of atmospheric seeing on visual astronomy and astrophotography is more dramatic than most amateur astronomers realize, and the numbers tell a sobering story.
The Impact of Seeing on Telescopes
On average, even at professional observatory sites, typical seeing is around
0.5 to 1.5 arcseconds
. For most amateur astronomers at typical locations, seeing often ranges from
2 to 4 arcseconds
[3]. This means that, regardless of
telescope size
, atmospheric turbulence usually limits the sharpness of your astrophotography images to a resolution of about 2–4 arcseconds—far less than what many modern telescopes are theoretically capable of achieving. In practical terms, this atmospheric blurring can reduce the effective resolution of a high-quality 8-inch (20 cm) telescope by more than 80% on an average night, making the atmosphere the dominant factor in image sharpness for most observers[3][1].
Sources
[1]
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronomical_seeing
[2]
https://skyandtelescope.org/astronomy-equipment/beating-the-seeing/
[3]
https://www.innovationsforesight.com/astronomical-seeing-tutorial/

different types of astrophotography
.
How Does Seeing Affect Your Images?

data.title: Uber's new shuttles look suspiciously familiar to anyone who's taken a bus
data.author: Improvement
data.article_summary: Uber最近推出了固定路线共享服务（Route Share），类似于公交系统，旨在提供更 affordable 和 predictable 的通勤选择。尽管公司声称此举有助于缓解拥堵和环境问题，但有专家指出，这种服务在环保和公共交通系统方面的效果存疑。研究显示，共享乘车服务往往增加碳排放，且可能替代更环保的出行方式，如步行和骑自行车。此外，公共交通系统因预算短缺和联邦支持减少而面临困境，而Uber等公司的介入可能进一步削弱公共交通的公益性和问责机制。专家担忧，这种商业模式可能导致公共交通私有化，并对依赖公共交通的低收入人群产生负面影响。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• 观点一：怀疑Uber关心上述问题的真实性。Meagher质疑Uber是否真正关心降低消费者价格、缓解交通拥堵和保护环境，暗示Uber的动机主要是商业利益，而非社会责任。
• 观点二：潜在支持Uber的目标。虽然没有明确表达，但假设Uber的声明是真诚的，其目标是减少消费者成本和改善环境。这种观点认为企业可能在追求利润的同时，也关注社会问题。

Every few years, a Silicon Valley gig-economy company announces a “disruptive” innovation that looks a whole lot like a bus. Uber rolled out Smart Routes a decade ago, followed a short time later by the Lyft Shuttle of its biggest competitor. Even Elon Musk gave it a try in 2018 with the “urban loop system” that never quite materialized
beyond the Vegas Strip
. And does anyone remember Chariot?
Now it’s Uber’s turn again. The ride-hailing company recently announced
Route Share
, in which shuttles will travel dozens of fixed routes, with fixed stops, picking up passengers and dropping them off at fixed times. Amid the inevitable jokes about Silicon Valley once again discovering buses are serious questions about what this will mean for struggling transit systems, air quality, and congestion.
Uber promised the program, which rolled out
in seven cities at the end of May, will bring “more affordable, more predictable” transportation during peak commuting hours.
“Many of our users, they live in generally the same area, they work in generally the same area, and they commute at the same time,” Sachin Kansal, the company’s chief product officer, said during the company’s May 14 announcement. “The concept of Route Share is not new,” he admitted — though he never used the word “bus.” Instead, pictures of horse-drawn buggies, rickshaws, and pedicabs appeared onscreen.

Here's How
CEO Dara Khosrowshahi was a bit more forthcoming when
he told The Verge
the whole thing is “to some extent inspired by the bus.” The goal, he said, “is just to reduce prices to the consumer and then help with congestion and the environment.”
But Kevin Shen, who studies this sort of thing at the Union of Concerned Scientists, questions whether Uber’s “next-gen bus” will do much for commuters or the climate. “Everybody will say, ‘Silicon Valley’s reinventing the bus again,’” Shen said. “But it’s more like they’re reinventing a worse bus.”
Five years ago, the Union of Concerned Scientists released a
report
that found ride-share services emit 69 percent more planet-warming carbon dioxide and other pollutants than the trips they displace — largely because as many as 40 percent of the miles traveled by Uber and Lyft drivers are driven without a passenger, something called “deadheading.” That climate disadvantage decreases with pooled services like UberX Share — but it’s still not much greener than owning and driving a vehicle, the report noted, unless
the car is electric
.
Beyond the iffy climate benefit lie broader concerns about what this means for the transit systems in New York, San Francisco, Chicago, Philadelphia, Dallas, Boston, and Baltimore — and the people who rely on them.

Here's How
“Transit is a public service, so a transit agency’s goal is to serve all of its customers, whether they’re rich or poor, whether it’s the maximum profit-inducing route or not,” Shen said. The entities that do all of this come with accountability mechanisms — boards, public meetings, vocal riders — to ensure they do what they’re supposed to. “Barely any of that is in place for Uber.” This, he said, is a pivot toward a public-transit model
without public accountability
.
Compounding the threat, Philadelphia and Dallas have struggling transit systems at risk of defunding. The situation is so dire in Philly that it may cut service by nearly 45 percent on July 1 amid a chronic financial crisis. (That, as one Reddit user pointed out,
would be good news for Uber
.)
Meanwhile, the federal government is cutting support for public services,
including transit systems
— many of which still haven’t fully recovered from COVID-era budget crunches. Though ridership nationwide is up to
85 percent of pre-pandemic levels
, Bloomberg News recently estimated that transit systems across the country face a
$6 billion budget shortfall
. So it’s easy to see why companies like Uber see a business opportunity in public transit.
Khosrowshahi insists Uber is “in competition with personal car ownership,” not public transportation. “Public transport is a teammate,” he told The Verge. But a
study
released last year by the University of California, Davis found that in three California cities, over half of all ride-hailing trips didn’t replace personal cars, they replaced more
sustainable modes of getting around
, like walking, public transportation, and bicycling.
And then there’s the fact cities like New York grapple with

and don’t need more vehicles cluttering cr

data.title: Radio for DuckDB – DuckDB Now Talks to WebSockets and Redis Pub/Sub
data.author: rustyconover
data.article_summary: Radio是由Query.Farm开发的DuckDB扩展，允许DuckDB与WebSocket和Redis发布/订阅服务器等实时事件系统交互。它支持接收和发送事件消息：接收的消息被缓存并可通过SQL查询，发出的消息被缓存并支持发送跟踪。Radio扩展引入了核心对象"radio"，可以管理多个事件源订阅，每个订阅有独立的连接和消息队列。扩展功能包括订阅管理、消息监听、接收和发送消息等。使用示例展示了如何连接WebSocket服务器并接收消息。Radio是DuckDB社区扩展，未来将支持更多事件源如Google PubSub和MQTT等。安装方式为：`INSTALL radio FROM community;` 然后加载：`LOAD radio;`。

44170755.article_content:
The
Radio
extension by
Query.Farm
enables DuckDB to interact with real-time event systems such as WebSocket and Redis Publish/Subscribe servers. It allows DuckDB to both
receive
and
send
events: incoming messages are buffered and queryable with SQL, while outgoing events are buffered and support delivery tracking.
The extension is named
Radio
because it effectively equips DuckDB with a two-way radioâallowing it to
listen for
and
broadcast
messages across event-driven systems.
Note
DuckDB extensions are modular plugins that enhance the core engine with powerful new capabilities like this.
Getting Started
Radio will be a
DuckDB community extension
maintained and supported by
Query.Farm
.
Install Radio in DuckDB by running:
INSTALL radio
FROM
community;
Then load it with:
LOAD radio;
Functionality
The
Radio
extension introduces a few core concepts.
At its core is a single
radio
object that manages multiple
subscriptions
to event sources. Think of the radio as being a radio that can listen to multiple broadcasts at the same time. The event sources that the radio extension can interact with include WebSocket servers and Redis publish/subscribe. Support for additional event systems will be added over time.
Tip
Additional event sources planned are: Google PubSub, Azure ServiceBus, MQTT / Mosquito, Subprocesses / Pipes.
If youâre interested in these additional event sources,
contact us
.
You can create multiple subscriptions to event sources, each subscription is indepent of other subscriptions. Each subscription has an independent connection to the event source and has a independent send and receive thread. Multiple subscriptions can exist simultaneously in the same DuckDB process (even to the same event source).
Every subscription maintains two internal queues:
Received messages
Messages to transmit
The received messages queue is size limited, as it fills up older messages are discarded based on the configured queue size. The size of the receive queue is configurable when the subcription is created.
Received messages have a field called
seen_count
which tracks the number of times the message has been seen by DuckDB. Newly received messages will have a
seen_count
of 1.
Architecture Diagram
This diagram shows the internal architecture of the extension and how it integrated into DuckDB.
Integration Flowchart
This flowchart shows which functions to use for each type of activity with the extension.
When Should I Use This?
Use the Radio extension when you want to
receive or send events
from a Websocket server or Redis Publish/Subscribe service within DuckDBâwithout needing external event-handling infrastructure or orchestration logic.
Hereâs an example of connecting to a WebSocket server and receiving messages:
-- Connect to the server
CALL
radio_subscribe(
'ws://127.0.0.1:20400'
);

data.title: Making maps with noise functions (2022)
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了使用噪声函数生成二维地图（如高度图和生物群系图）的基本方法，特别强调了利用Simplex或Perlin噪声函数生成地形。文章首先解释了如何通过循环填充一个数组，并用噪声值生成基础地图。接着讨论了频率对地形细节的影响，提出通过调整频率和波长来控制地形的缩放。为增加地形的复杂性，文章引入了多个频率的噪声叠加，即“倍频”或“八度”，并通过调整振幅使地形更接近自然界的分形结构。最后，文章提到可以动态调整振幅以优化地形生成，提供了实现更复杂地形的思路。

主要讨论点：关于一份程序生成指南的评价及其应用

不同观点：
• [hexator] 认为该指南是该领域中最具权威性的指南，尤其在程序生成社区中非常有名。这表明该指南被视为高品质和具有影响力的资源。

• [ryan42] 赞同指南的详细解释，并表示正着手在Godot引擎中开发游戏，可能会尝试将指南中的方法应用到自己的项目中。他还提到《Realm of the Mad God》是一款很棒的游戏，暗示该指南可能对类似游戏开发有帮助。

• [sebnado] 肯定了指南在程序地图生成方面的优点，但指出如果目标是实现真实感，可能需要像Gaea这样的工具。这暗示了该指南在某些追求高真实感的场景中可能不够用。

补充讨论：
• 关于指南的应用场景存在不同看法。[hexator]和[ryan42]更关注指南在游戏开发和程序生成方面的价值，而[sebnado]则提到了指南在追求更高真实感图形生成方面的局限性，推荐了Gaea作为更合适的工具。

• 争议的焦点在于指南的适用范围。虽然[hexator]和[ryan42]对其在程序生成中的作用持积极态度，但[sebnado]指出了其在某些特定领域（如追求真实感）中的不足。

• 评论中也提到了具体工具的应用，如Godot引擎和Gaea，这些工具在不同开发需求下被推荐和比较，进一步丰富了对指南应用场景的讨论。
